restoration_note: The teaching presents an anatomy of the body as a twelve-gated dragon (seven sense-organs of head + five lower caves) and defines the Virgin/Continent as the soul that recognizes and conquers this dragon (= enthumesis of the body / Hyle). Most gaps are tightly constrained: visible Coptic letters, line-break splits of single words (ⲡⲕⲉⲗⲉⲥ, ⲡⲥⲱⲙⲁ, ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ, ⲡⲥⲛⲁϩ, ⲍⲱⲧⲃⲉ, ⲙⲛⲧⲉϩⲧⲉ), and parallel formulas (ⲧⲥⲁϣϩⲃⲉ ⲛ̄ⲁⲡⲉ, ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲕⲱⲛ, ⲡⲙⲁⲍ-N ⲡⲉ enumeration). The five caves are restored from the visible enumeration: tongue, throat, heart, breath, and the bond (ⲡⲥⲛⲁϩ — likely the navel-cord or generative bond). The body-member list at L34 (gaps {23}, {24}) and the fragmentary L35 ({25}, {26}) are too damaged to restore: the body's seven-fold members between the haunches cannot be specified without parallels in this corpus, and the bare ⲁⲣⲭⲱⲛ at L35 has no preserved edge. Gap {0} (3 chars before ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲉϩⲧⲉ) and {13} (the singular tongue's qualifier between sense-pairs and the relative clause) are proposed with low confidence as the grammar permits but no strong parallel fixes them.
